changes: First RINGMOD SC release: an insert whose gain follows another track's audio. DUCK pulls the gain down with the key's peak over the last one to two HOLD windows (13-26 ms by default), so it holds through a kick's zero crossings and steps down as it decays; ATK softens the fall and REL the recovery. RING multiplies the audio by the key, a ring modulator whose carrier is any of T1-T8. Main page: KEY (OFF, T1-T8), DPTH and KLPF over ATK, HOLD and REL; MODE (DUCK, RING) on SETUP. DPTH 0 or KEY OFF passes the audio bit for bit.

In RING the three DUCK knobs shape the carrier and are named SLEW, S&H and BIAS there: S&H takes a new key every 16 samples a step and holds it between (stepped modulation); SLEW above 0 drives the gain with the key's level, smoothed from 0.7 ms to 1.3 s, a tremolo that follows the key; BIAS keeps up to half the dry signal under the modulation, from ring modulation at 0 to amplitude modulation at 127, ramped so it does not click. At 0 each is a plain copy, so RING with all three at 0 is the plain ring modulator; the knobs keep their values when MODE changes, so turn S&H and BIAS to 0 after switching a fresh instance to RING.

It reads the Modwerk base's key bus over USB (loader ABI 9, requires the key bus): no tap of its own and nothing written outside its own state, so it runs beside Sidechain Compressor. While it is installed the base's tap copies every track on both cores, and its price (41 executed instructions a sample a core, counted from the source, charged at 7/4) counts toward RINGMOD SC. A card image has no key bus: there it keeps its depth at 0 and passes the audio untouched (the card configurator still offers it until the site's USB-only rule lands).

Key latency is the bus's: exact from a track dispatched earlier on the same core, 16 samples from one dispatched later, 32 across the cores (measured on an MKII for Sidechain Compressor and on the key bus re-check, not yet as heard through this module). 322 DSP words, 20 words of state, no buffer; 63 instructions a sample in either mode by static count; 80.56 executed instructions a sample at worst measured (DUCK with a trig split; RING 76.44).

Hardware: the 0.1.0 build (never published), whose DUCK and plain RING this version reproduces sample for sample, passed its first MKII steps over USB on 21 October 2026: the key bus, install and charge, KEY's labels and steps, and DUCK by ear (DPTH 0 and KEY OFF untouched; KLPF, HOLD, ATK and REL act). Limits: SLEW, S&H and BIAS have not run on a unit; DUCK buzzes at its very shortest ATK, HOLD and REL (audio-rate amplitude modulation, as expected); on the first visit to the main page KEY may move a track a detent (card images under the emulator); installing Sidechain Compressor while it is live re-zeroes the bus once, about a block of silent key. Scenes, project save, Part reload and a power cycle are untested.
